findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh stage-layouts apt-get install line and expect_output_has "today's libraries pass the written floor" "highest=GLIBC_2.38"
findings.obligation: Obligation (a): today build passes the floor and the highest GLIBC version is parsed; design expects highest=GLIBC_2.38
findings.observation: The WebKit package is installed unpinned (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0) from a moving archive; the image digest pins the base only. An exact GLIBC_2.38 pin turns an archive update that still satisfies the floor into a false red, not a silent pass. Medium.
findings.remediation: Pin the package version in stage-layouts, or derive the expected highest independently by running readelf -V in the oracle and compare; keep requiring a non-empty parsed highest version.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh lines 354-365 (line_number_of check-glibc-floor.sh on the workflow file)
findings.obligation: Promise P2 and Expectation E4: CI fails a build whose AppImage needs a newer glibc than the floor, so it is never released
findings.observation: The check is a static order of first-occurrence line numbers. A comment naming check-glibc-floor.sh satisfies it. The oracle does not require a run: step, does not reject continue-on-error, and does not require the extracted squashfs-root argument, so a floor step that cannot fail the job passes. Medium.
findings.remediation: Parse the workflow YAML (actionlint is available) and assert that the step between the libssl step and the upload step has a run invoking check-glibc-floor.sh on the extracted directory, with no continue-on-error. Keep the order check on step indexes, not first-occurrence lines.

findings.obligation: Design: the packaging run installs readelf through binutils
findings.observation: A bare word match passes on a comment. Low.
findings.remediation: Assert binutils appears on an apt install run line of the workflow, e.g. by parsing the YAML step that runs apt-get install.

findings.obligation: Inspect each oracle measured RED: the missing behaviour must show a semantic RED
findings.observation: Sixteen FAIL lines are exit code was 127 with bash: /tools/check-glibc-floor.sh: No such file. The RED is valid because the script is CreateNew, but it reads as tool-not-found rather than behaviour absent. Low.
findings.remediation: Add one explicit existence check for tools/linux-appimage/check-glibc-floor.sh that reports WHAT: the floor check is not written, WHY, HOW, and state the cause in each exit assertion. Re-review that delta only.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh cases missing directory, no-ELF directory, and the refusal blocks
findings.obligation: Failures B1 (exit 2 naming what could not be read) and B2 (WHAT, WHY, HOW per offending file)
findings.observation: B1 cases assert exit 2 only; they do not assert the output names the unreadable directory. B2 asserts WHAT and WHY content but never asserts a HOW label. Low.
findings.remediation: Assert the output names the directory for the missing and no-ELF cases, and that each refusal block carries WHAT, WHY and HOW labels (structure only, not prose).

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh cases needs_2_9 through needs_2_100, offender, no-version-needs fixtures; build-fixtures.sh
findings.obligation: Constructibility of the real ELF fixtures for L1, L2, L4 and B5 (failing setup must not look like RED)
findings.observation: Setup succeeded (gcc links ran) but the oracle does not check the fixture version needs. A stub libc that records no version, or a stripped section that still reports versions, would turn a fixture defect into a false RED or false PASS. The review could not read readelf output (see R4). Low.
findings.remediation: Add a setup self-check in the oracle: needs_2_40 lists GLIBC_2.40, offender lists GLIBC_2.42, no-version-needs lists no GLIBC_ entry; a failure is setup_failed. Show these readelf lines on the first GREEN run.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh cut-off case: expect_exit "a cut-off ELF file is not a pass" 2
findings.obligation: Failure B5 and the silent-pass rule: an ELF whose needs cannot be read exits 2 naming the file
findings.observation: Only the exit code and the file name are pinned. A wrong fix that exits 2 on any readelf stderr also passes this case, and no existing layout has a healthy file that makes readelf warn, so nothing refuses that fix. Medium.
findings.remediation: Add a healthy-but-warning fixture, an ELF whose readelf -V prints a warning on stderr while its GLIBC needs are complete, with the spec outcome stated: exit by its needs, not by stderr. Keep the cut-off case as is.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh mode-000 case: /layouts/unreadable, and no mixed layout
findings.obligation: Silent-pass rule for unopenable files; and the AppImage promise that non-ELF content is not a refusal
findings.observation: The case pins exit 2 for an unopenable ELF. A fix that exits 2 on any non-ELF or unopenable file also passes it, and no layout mixes a text or PNG file with clean ELF files, so that fix would refuse a real AppImage that ships desktop or icon files. Medium.
findings.remediation: Add a layout with a non-ELF file (text and PNG) beside clean ELF files expecting exit 0 or 1 by the ELF needs alone. Keep the mode-000 case to an ELF file only.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh expect_output_has "a floor of 2." "WHAT" and the quoted-value checks
findings.obligation: Floor validation: a non-dotted floor exits 2 with WHAT naming the value
findings.observation: The WHAT check is satisfied by offender blocks from real libraries printed in the run, not by a floor refusal. The quoted-value check accepts any output containing the value, including a file path. A fix that prints offender blocks and exits 2 without naming the floor passes. Low.
findings.remediation: Assert a floor-refusal WHAT line that contains the quoted value, and assert the output has no per-file offender block. Add a three-part floor case, 2.39.1, expected to be accepted.
